region.text: Chiang Rai province: Chiang Saen, Mae Sai and the Kok River, 'the upper Mekong basin' where the polity flourished

ledger.note: 638: Lao Chakkaraj makes Hiran Nakhon his chief seat. 'He rebuilt the city and made it his chief seat in 638 under the name Hiran Nakhon', 'traditionally regarded as marking the inception of the Ngoenyang Kingdom'. The founding is a chronicle tradition (the reign of over a hundred years 'is considered chronologically problematic').

region.text: the southern part in the Ping River basin, split off in 662 as Haripunjaya

ledger.note: 662: the Ping basin splits off. 'In 662, the southern part in the Ping River Basin was split off and became the Haripuñjaya Kingdom.' The haripunjaya dossier starts that state c. 750 (its own page: 'the actual beginning is placed at around 750').

region.text: Phukamyao, the Phayao basin around Wiang Phayao

ledger.note: 1094: Phayao secedes. Infobox 'Secession of Phayao: 1094'; Prince Khun Chomtham, 'culminating in the re-establishment of a new center identified as the Phayao Kingdom'. The Phayao dossier founds its kingdom in 1094.

region.text: Thoeng and Chiang Kham, taken from Phayao by Mangrai (undated; the Phayao dossier's circle)

ledger.note: c. 1261: Mangrai takes Thoeng and Chiang Kham from Phayao. The Mangrai page lists the conquest of 'Muang Lai, Chiang Khong, Chiang Kham, and Thoeng, the last two of which belonged to Phayao' without a date; 1261 is the phayao-kingdom dossier's bridge to Mangrai's accession.

1262: Mangrai founds Chiang Rai. 'In 1262, he founded the city of Chiang Rai as his new capital in the Kok River basin' (the Ngoenyang page: Mangrai ascended in 1262 as the 25th ruler; Baker and Phongpaichit date the founding to 1263).
1275: the court at Fang. The Ngoenyang infobox lists 'Fang (1275-1286)'; the Mangrai page puts him in the Fang area 'around' 1262 and gives no 1275.

1286: Wiang Kum Kam (infobox 'Wiang Kum Kam (1286-1292)'). The Mangrai page says 'In 1294, Wiang Kum Kam was founded' and the Ping basin was Mon until 1291-92, so this move rests on one page against the other.

region.text: Mangrai's Ngoenyang, which becomes Lan Na

ledger.note: 1292: Mangrai's Ngoenyang becomes the Lan Na kingdom. Infobox 'Foundation of Lanna: 1292', 'Succeeded by: Lan Na; Phayao'. The conquest of Haripunjaya is dated 1281 (Ngoenyang infobox), 1291 (Mangrai page: 'In 1291 ... Mangrai defeated the Mon kingdom') and 1292 (Lan Na and Haripunjaya dossiers), and sits in lan-na-kingdom's ledger.

certainty.note: A mandala kingdom: the page gives cities and basins, never a frontier.

notes: State Cliopatria lacks; needed as the counterpart of lan-na-kingdom (found 1292), phayao-kingdom (found 1094, 1261 loss) and haripunjaya. Two pages opened. Not settled: (1) the founding in 638 is chronicle tradition and the 25-ruler list (reigns over a century) is unreliable, so no ruler strip is given; (2) the 662 split of Haripunjaya contradicts the haripunjaya dossier's c. 750 start (and the legendary 629), leaving the Ping basin unowned 662-749 if both are followed; Cliopatria's Haripuñjaya shape starts 666; (3) the date of Mangrai's conquest of Haripunjaya: 1281 (Ngoenyang infobox), 1291 (Mangrai page), 1292 (Lan Na and Haripunjaya dossiers); it is left to lan-na-kingdom and haripunjaya, and Ngoenyang is not drawn with Haripunjaya before 1292; (4) the capital sequence conflicts with the Mangrai page on Wiang Kum Kam (1286 against 1294) and on Fang (1275 against about 1262); (5) Nanzhao influence late 8th to late 9th century and the Thai-Lao migrations are not territory; (6) the Ngoenyang page is silent on Khmer relations and on area. A page for Yonok and Wiang Prueksa (predecessors in the infobox) was not opened.
